messages:
Maria Chen: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC rollout — nightly bench saw a p99 jump on the attn-heavy suite after rolling kernel_v2. Not huge overall but tail widened. Anyone else noticing this?
Kevin Park: saw it too, noticed p999 is the worst. p50/p90 unchanged.
bench-bot: nightly-run 1893410000 -> kernel_v2 diff: p50 +0.0%, p90 +0.4%, p99 +3.6%, p999 +12.2%. sample N=18,432 requests. Link: https://bench.redwood/1893410000
Sanjay Rao: probable suspects: new fused-attn path + different kernel scheduling -> occasional context-switching at long sequences. Also check KV-cache invalidation behavior.
Helen Ortiz: can you post the representative input distribution? if the tail is sequences > 2048 it's expected. If not, we may have a correctness/queueing issue.
Maria Chen: sample distribution pasted from the nightly harness: 
```
seq_len histogram: 1-128: 58%, 129-512: 28%, 513-2048: 11%, >2048: 3%
workload: chat-like with many short prompts + a small set of long documents
```
Kevin Park: thanks. p999 spike doesn't map cleanly to >2048 bucket. I ran a quick microbench on single-gpu with same kernel and saw rare spikes when concurrent QKV builds overlapped. Could be a lock/priority inversion.
Lee Nguyen: I've seen that pattern when the kernel selector falls back to a compatibility kernel under memory pressure — fallback path has different batching semantics and can inflate tail. Are we falling back often?
bench-bot: runtime logs show 0.8% requests hit compatibility fallback during the window (timestamp range 1893419000-1893420000).
Sanjay Rao: 0.8% fallback + a tiny fraction of long sequences could explain p999 12% delta. hypothesis: fallback triggers extra memcpy + serialization overhead.
Helen Ortiz: can we reproduce locally? Maria, can you schedule a reproducer with a seeded mix: 60% short, 37% medium, 3% long plus 1% artificially force fallback? Use this harness: 
```
./harness --mix 60,37,3 --force-fallback=1 --concurrency 64 --duration 5m
```
Maria Chen: scheduling now. I'll also add tracing at kernel-selection layer and kvcache events.
ci-bot: CI perf job queued: perf/repro/1893421120-try1 — will post results when done.
Kevin Park: small methodology note — our p99 calculation merges per-worker histograms then computes quantiles. That amplifies tiny fallback tails. For triage, please also report raw event counts and a bootstrapped CI on quantiles.
Maria Chen: agreed. I'll include raw latencies and bootstrap 95% CI.
bench-bot: repro run complete. Summary: p50 12ms, p90 18ms, p99 42ms, p999 128ms. Fallback hits 1.1% during run. Logs: 
```
[1893422605] kernel-selection: selected fused_attn_v2
[1893422609] kernel-selection: fallback -> compat_attn (mem-pressure)
[1893422612] compat-attn: memcpy 6.3ms
```
Lee Nguyen: that memcpy number is suspicious — compat path seems to copy per-token buffers instead of in-place. We need to inspect compat_attn implementation.
Sanjay Rao: two actionable tracks: (1) short-term: adjust selector to avoid compat fallback when concurrency high by preferring slightly higher memory headroom; (2) long-term: refactor compat_attn to reuse buffers or implement zero-copy path.
Helen Ortiz: add a test that simulates memory pressure + concurrency and asserts no >50ms tail regression. Also add telemetry: tag requests that hit fallback so dashboards can filter.
Maria Chen: owner assignments — Kevin: instrument selector metrics + bootstrapped quantiles; Lee: dig into compat_attn memcpy; Sanjay: prototype selector-change; Helen: add test + telemetry tag. I'll open a follow-up RFC with proposed selector change and risk matrix.
Kevin Park: ack. I'll upload initial metrics PR by EOD.
Lee Nguyen: I'll start a compat_attn branch and try removing the extra memcpy.
Sanjay Rao: prototyping selector change now, will run canary with reduced fallback threshold.
bench-bot: tagging the nightly regression ticket: RG-2026-1893421120.
Maria Chen: thanks all. Will update thread after the canary run. :thumbsup:
